heroLead: Arnot is a former coal-mining community in Tioga County, a small place with a mining history that predates the Marcellus boom by well over a century.
intro: Arnot was centered on coal mining back in the 1800s, one of many small company towns that once dotted this part of Tioga County. That older coal history means some family land here may have a mineral estate that was split apart generations ago, coal going one direction, oil and gas potentially staying with the original family, depending on exactly how the old deeds were written.
We take the time to trace that history properly, because getting it wrong means either overpaying for rights you don't actually control or underpaying because nobody bothered to check.

sections.heading: An old coal patch in the dry-gas Marcellus core
paragraphs: Tioga County sits within the strong dry-gas window of the northeastern Marcellus play, and while Arnot's own coal-era history is older, much of the surrounding township has been leased for gas development over the past fifteen or so years. If your family's oil and gas rights survived the earlier coal severance intact, you may hold a real interest in current or future Marcellus production.
Tioga County also includes significant state forest land, and operators have worked with both private landowners and state agencies to develop leasehold across the county's productive core.

sections.heading: Confirming what survived the coal era
paragraphs: We trace your chain of title through the Tioga County Recorder of Deeds, checking specifically what any historical coal severance covered and what it left with the family, before evaluating current oil and gas rights.

sections.heading: What we offer once ownership is clear
paragraphs: Once your interest is confirmed, we check current leasing and production status tied to your parcel and put together a number that reflects what you actually, legally hold today.

faqs.question: Did the old coal mining near Arnot affect our family's oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific deed language from that era. We'll trace the historical severance to confirm exactly what was and wasn't included.

faqs.question: Is there active gas leasing near Arnot today?
faqs.answer: Tioga County has substantial dry-gas Marcellus development, though specific activity varies by parcel. We'll confirm what applies to your tract.

faqs.question: What if my land borders state forest land?
faqs.answer: That doesn't affect your private mineral rights, though it can influence how a unit is configured. We'll explain how it applies to your specific situation.
